blocks.text: This book was written to transmit a foundation. To do that it needed language, examples, stories across many domains. That was necessary. It also carries a risk worth naming honestly.

Resonance can stop at the examples. A reader who recognizes themselves in a story may feel they have understood. They have found the door. The door is not the destination. The destination is the attending, the hand on the chest, the raw report before the story about it forms.

The lens is a reading tool. It describes what the pulse does. Consistency with the lens is not the same as truth. A reading that coheres with the framework is worth examining. It is not therefore correct. When a claim can no longer be pointed to in something observable and only appears through the lens, slow down. Return to what is actually there.

Conversation is the correction mechanism. What one dot cannot see alone becomes visible through genuine exchange. The drift matters less than the return. Resonance that holds under pressure is different from resonance that has never been tested.
Try the lens in conversation. Show your reading to someone you trust. Ask whether it matches what they see.
Tools don't apologize for working. A hammer drives a nail or it doesn't. A saw cuts or it doesn't. You don't ask the hammer to prove its ontology. You try it on the wood.
The lens works the same way. Try it. If it helps you see, use it. If it doesn't, set it down.

Every tool needs a language. This one uses colors: blue for expansion, red for contraction, green for balance. That language is not the truth. It is a way of describing what the pulse does. The description is impartial. It does not prefer faith over science. It does not prefer blue over red. It watches. It names. It asks one question: does this pulse remember where it lives?
My explanations of the lens might be wrong. I am a person who fragmented and rebuilt. I see what I see. Another person might see differently. That is fine.

But the reading itself, the act of attending to your pulse, of noticing when you expand and when you contract, of asking what the container needs, that is not mine. That belongs to anyone with a hand to place on their chest.
So take the lens. Use the language. Test the reading against your own container.
If it doesn't, you have lost nothing.
